title: Public-API window-move tracking: AX observers + activeSpaceDidChange
description:
Immediate fix for the stale-cache phantom-border bug (focusfx-l4i). Implements push-based window-state updates using only public APIs, so AeroSpace workspace switches and Mission Control Space switches refresh the WindowTracker cache without polling.

What:
1. Subscribe to NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification — on fire, call WindowTracker.refresh() (re-enumerates and diff-coalesces).
2. For each running app with windows in the cache, install an AXObserver and register kAXWindowMovedNotification, kAXWindowResizedNotification, kAXWindowMiniaturizedNotification, kAXWindowDeminiaturizedNotification, and kAXFocusedWindowChangedNotification per AX window. On notification, push the affected window's new frame through the existing coalescer (or trigger a targeted re-read for that window).
3. Lifecycle: track AX observers in a [pid: AXObserver] map; install on NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification, tear down on didTerminateApplicationNotification. Re-attach observers when refresh() discovers new windows.

Why:
- AeroSpace's hideInCorner moves frames without changing frontmost app, so didActivateApplication misses these events. AX move events fire on every frame change including AeroSpace's teleportation.
- Native macOS Space switches publish activeSpaceDidChange (public NSWorkspace notification). This catches Mission Control / Stage Manager moves without needing SLS.
- Combined, this covers both phantom-border failure modes today using public APIs only.

How:
- Extend WindowTracker.installWorkspaceObservers() to add the activeSpaceDidChange observer and the launch/terminate observers.
- New WindowTracker.AXObserverManager (or inline) handles per-pid AX observer lifecycle.
- AX callbacks hop to the trackerQueue, build a CoalescedUpdate, and bump generation through the existing coalescer pathway.
- Skip apps that don't expose AX windows (silent — AccessibilityStatus already gates the daemon-wide failure mode).

Acceptance:
- After AeroSpace workspace switch with frontmost app unchanged, BorderEngine recomputes within one coalesce tick (~16ms).
- After Mission Control Space switch, cache reflects the new active Space's windows within one tick.
- No measurable idle CPU regression vs current baseline (AX observers are push, not polled).
- Unit tests for AXObserver wiring (or integration test driven by stub AXBridge that simulates move events).

Dependencies: focusfx-l4i (bug this fixes).
Blocks: focusfx-30 (v0 hardening — phantom borders are a release blocker).

Notes:
- Once focusfx-b13 (SLS streaming) lands, the AX observers can be removed for apps where SLS is authoritative, but activeSpaceDidChange stays as a robust public-API path.
- Do NOT add a polling timer fallback — it conflicts with the < 1% idle CPU release goal.
close_reason: AXWindowObserverManager + activeSpaceDidChange landed. AX observers attach per-pid for app-level Created/FocusedWindowChanged/Activated/Deactivated and per-window Moved/Resized/Miniaturized/Deminiaturized/UIElementDestroyed. NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChange wired alongside didActivateApplication. Burst of AX events collapses to one re-enumeration via 16ms debouncer. NoopAXWindowObserverManager available for tests; existing tracker tests updated. 3 new tests + 114 total all green; live-built and running.

title: Phantom borders after AeroSpace workspace switch (stale cache)
description:
WindowTracker only refreshes on NSWorkspace.didActivateApplicationNotification + initial enumeration. AeroSpace switches workspaces by moving window frames (hideInCorner: bottomLeftCorner - (W,0) or bottomRightCorner ± 1px) WITHOUT triggering app activation when the frontmost app stays the same. Result: cached frames go stale, BorderEngine keeps drawing borders at the previous workspace's frame positions, producing phantom borders mid-screen.

Reproduce: open two AeroSpace workspaces both holding a Warp window, focus a Warp window in workspace A, switch to workspace B. Border for the workspace-A Warp window stays drawn at its old frame.

Verified via: Sources/LimeCore/WindowTracking/WindowTracker.swift:55,202 — only refresh path is didActivateApplication. CGWindowListBridge.isStreaming=false (Sources/LimeCore/WindowTracking/WindowServerBridge.swift:20).

JankyBorders does not have this issue because it subscribes to SkyLight events (move=806, resize=807, reorder=808, hide/unhide=815/816, create/destroy=1325/1326, space-change=1401, front-app=1508 — see JankyBorders/src/events.c:113) and refreshes current-space windows on space change.

Tinkle is not a counterexample — it observes AX focusedWindowChanged for transient effects only and does not need to track non-focused windows.

Fix is split across two issues:
- Immediate public-API fix: see follow-up issue (AX move/resize observers + activeSpaceDidChange).
- Structural fix: focusfx-b13 (SLS streaming bridge).

title: Filter non-app windows from border enumeration
description:
Bug found in v0 borders QA: every CGWindowList tick re-enumerated our own border overlays (level statusBar+1) plus menu-bar items, status items, and popovers. Result: double-bordering, borders on menu bar items, and exploding window count between launches (59 → 123).

Fix: parseEntry rejects layer != 0 and alpha <= 0; BorderRenderer sets sharingType=.none on overlay windows as defense in depth. 6 unit tests cover layer 0/3/25/26 + zero-alpha rejection.

Verified live: window count dropped from 123 to 46 after fix on the same desktop.
close_reason: Fixed via layer/alpha filter in CGWindowListBridge.parseEntry + sharingType=.none on BorderRenderer. 111/111 tests green; live window count 123→46.

title: Filter borders to AX-owned windows only
description: Apps like Arc expose multiple CGWindow entries per user-visible window (chrome/toolbar/content as separate NSWindows). Occlusion alone can't dedupe them since each has a distinct non-overlapping frame, leading to stacked borders on Arc that don't appear on simpler apps like Slack. Solution: cross-reference cache against each pid's AX kAXWindowsAttribute. Only windows the app itself reports as user-visible get bordered. Implementation: AXBridge.axWindowIDs(for:) returns Set<CGWindowID>; WindowTracker populates per pid during enumeration; BorderEngineLogic filters by membership. Degrade gracefully if AX query fails (keep window — never lose borders due to AX hiccup).

title: Resolve focused window via _AXUIElementGetWindow
description: Multiple cache entries with empty CGWindow titles for the same pid (e.g. main Arc + Little Arc) cause focus to mis-resolve via the title/z-order tie-break in WindowTracker.recomputeFocus. Use _AXUIElementGetWindow (resolved via dlsym for graceful degradation) to map the AX focused element directly to a CGWindowID, eliminating the ambiguity. Falls back to today's title/z-order path if the symbol is unavailable.

title: Occlusion filter on focused-monitor borders
description: Hybrid design emits per-window borders for every visible window on the focused monitor. With z-stacked windows (e.g. multiple Slack windows in AeroSpace floating), all of them get bordered, producing overlapping lines. Walk orderedWindows front-to-back and skip any window whose frame intersects an already-accepted higher-z window's frame. Use exclusive intersect so AeroSpace pixel-adjacent tiles still pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hybrid per-monitor border design
description: Replace strict-occlusion with hybrid per-monitor design. Focused monitor: per-window borders (focused=active, others=inactive, preserving AeroSpace tile UX). Unfocused monitors: single screen-wide grey border at NSScreen.visibleFrame. Suppress on fullscreen monitors. Hide all screen borders on focusedWindowID==nil. Identify monitors by CGDirectDisplayID. 75ms debounce on focused-monitor swap. Wire didChangeScreenParametersNotification. Add Stage Manager note.

title: Add rich border styles: glow, gradient, background fill
description: Whole-plan context: focusfx-14.1 ships solid round/square borders only — ~80% of JankyBorders' day-to-day value with zero animation cost. Glow, gradient, and background-fill (the optional opaque surface behind a window) are deferred so the v0 BorderEngine ships clean. What: Implement the remaining ColorSpec cases in BorderRenderer — .glow uses CALayer.shadowColor/Path/Radius (or CIFilter behind), .gradient uses CAGradientLayer with the parsed top_left/bottom_right (or top_right/bottom_left) axis, and BordersConfig.background.enabled=true creates a separate fill window per target. ColorSpec already parses all three; the work is purely the renderer side. Why: Full JankyBorders parity for users who configured glow=glow(0xff...) or gradient(...). How: Extend BorderRenderer.applyColor to switch on ColorSpec; gradient/glow share the same NSWindow but swap the CALayer subclass; background fill window is its own NSWindow at order=below the target. Reuse existing coalescer hookup — no new event source. Verify idle CPU stays unchanged (no implicit animation loops).
acceptance_criteria: ColorSpec.glow renders with halo. ColorSpec.gradient renders with both axis variants. BordersConfig.background.enabled=true paints fill window. Idle CPU still 0% with rich styles applied.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add SLS streaming events + dlopen/dlsym private-API resolution
description: Whole-plan context: WindowTracker currently relies on CGWindowList for snapshots and NSWorkspace.didActivateApplication-driven re-enumeration for focus tracking. PLAN.md targets streaming SLS events for create/destroy/move/resize/order with idle CPU near zero. What: Add a streaming WindowServerBridge implementation backed by SLSRegisterNotifyProc / SLS event queue, with all private-API symbols resolved at runtime via dlopen+dlsym so a missing/renamed symbol degrades to the public-API bridge instead of crashing. Why: Per-event updates remove the implicit polling cost of the current refresh model, and dlsym-based resolution keeps us safe across macOS minor revisions where private symbols change. How: dlopen /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SkyLight.framework/SkyLight; resolve SLSMainConnectionID, SLSRegisterNotifyProc, SLSGetWindowBounds, SLSGetWindowOwner, etc. into function-pointer typedefs already declared in CSkyLight.h; build a StreamingSkyLightBridge that wraps them; on any dlsym miss, log fault and fall back to CGWindowListBridge while still answering enumerateOnScreenWindows().
acceptance_criteria: Streaming bridge reports per-window create/destroy/move/resize on the tracker queue. Missing/renamed private symbol does not crash; falls back to public bridge. WindowTracker.refresh() becomes optional rather than the primary update path.
notes:
SLS event class IDs to subscribe to (verified against JankyBorders/src/events.c:113):
  EVENT_WINDOW_MOVE      = 806
  EVENT_WINDOW_RESIZE    = 807
  EVENT_WINDOW_REORDER   = 808
  EVENT_WINDOW_HIDE      = 815
  EVENT_WINDOW_UNHIDE    = 816
  EVENT_WINDOW_CREATE    = 1325
  EVENT_WINDOW_DESTROY   = 1326
  EVENT_SPACE_CHANGE     = 1401
  EVENT_FRONT_APP_CHANGE = 1508

Symbols to dlsym from /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SkyLight.framework/SkyLight:
  SLSMainConnectionID, SLSRegisterNotifyProc (for events),
  SLSCopyManagedDisplays, SLSManagedDisplayGetCurrentSpace,
  SLSCopyWindowsWithOptionsAndTags (for current-space window enumeration),
  SLSWindowQueryWindows, SLSWindowQueryResultCopyWindows,
  SLSWindowIteratorAdvance, SLSWindowIteratorGetWindowID,
  SLSGetWindowBounds, SLSGetWindowOwner, SLSConnectionGetPID.

Once landed: the AX-observer plumbing in focusfx-1hr can be removed for apps where SLS streaming is authoritative; activeSpaceDidChange listener is kept as a public-API fallback.

title: Add event coalescing generation guards

Merge rules: destroyed always wins, created stays created through later changes. Single asyncAfter per coalescing window — N enqueues → 1 delivery. Queue bounded by distinct windows touched (10k events for 5 windows → pendingCount=5). Wired into WindowTracker: refresh() diffs old vs new cache and emits per-window create/destroy/frameChanged/visibilityChanged events; updateFocus() emits focusChanged for both losing-focus and gaining-focus windows. tracker.generation(for:) exposed for async border/effect work to stale-check before applying. 10 new tests (69 total) pass.

title: Background fill window (needs SLS)
description: Background fill (BordersConfig.background.enabled=true) paints an opaque rect under the target window. Until then BordersConfig.background.enabled is a no-op in the renderer; the daemon accepts the field but logs that fill is unsupported.

title: Defense-in-depth: drop borders for off-monitor parked windows
description:
Guardrail filter, NOT a primary fix. Even with push-based window-move events (focusfx-1hr) or SLS streaming (focusfx-b13), there can be a brief window between a frame-change event firing and our cache updating. During that window we still draw borders at stale frames. Add a cheap engine-side filter that drops any window whose frame center is not contained in the union of NSScreen.screens visible frames.

What: BorderEngine.recompute() snapshots NSScreen.screens.map { $0.frame } on the main hop it already does for primaryDisplayHeight. Pass through Inputs.visibleDisplayFrames. BorderEngineLogic.desiredBorders skips any window where no display rect contains CGPoint(frame.midX, frame.midY).

Why:
- Cheap (a few rect-contains checks per recompute, no API surface).
- Catches stale frames that have been parked far off-monitor by AeroSpace's hideInCorner before our cache refreshes.
- Handles other tilers using similar park-off-monitor tricks for free.
- Pure logic, fully testable.

Why this is ONLY a guardrail:
- It's a heuristic — center-on-display is not a definitive answer to 'visible to user'.
- It does NOT fix the root cause; if the cache is stale, we'll still see frames flicker correctly-then-incorrectly until the move event lands.
- Should not be relied on as the primary mechanism. focusfx-1hr and focusfx-b13 are the structural fixes.

Acceptance:
- Window with center outside all NSScreen.screens frames produces no border.
- Window with center inside at least one display rect is bordered (regardless of overlap with chrome / dock).
- Unit tests covering: single-display center-in / center-out; multi-display center-on-secondary; AeroSpace-parked frame at (-W, 0) → dropped.

Dependencies: none (purely additive). Lower priority than focusfx-1hr (does not fix the bug, just bounds its visible duration).

title: Stable dev-time accessibility permission (codesign / TCC ergonomics)
description: Whole-plan context: TCC tracks accessibility permission by code-signing identity. For ad-hoc / unsigned binaries (current dev setup) macOS uses cdhash, so every `swift build` rebuild changes the hash → permission re-prompts. This is a paper cut during borders/effects iteration but not a v0 release blocker. What: Investigate and document the developer workflow that minimizes re-prompting. Options: (1) self-signed certificate stored in login keychain + Scripts/bundle-app.sh codesigns with --sign $LIME_DEV_IDENTITY; (2) install the bundled .app to /Applications/LimeLight.app once and have devs run that path while iterating on the executable inside; (3) a Scripts/reset-tcc.sh one-liner that does `sudo tccutil reset Accessibility dev.abhirup.lime` so developers can re-prompt cleanly when needed. Why: Smoother dev loop. How: pick the lightest-touch option (likely #1 + #3 together).
acceptance_criteria: Documented dev workflow that survives ≥5 rebuilds without re-prompting (or a one-command reset path). Helper script in Scripts/ if needed.

title: Add border animations: focus-change crossfade, frame-change tween
description: Whole-plan context: focusfx-14.1 ships static borders that snap to new geometry/color on every coalesced tick. Smooth visual polish (cross-fading active↔inactive on focus change, tweening frame on resize/move) is a v1 enhancement. What: CABasicAnimation on borderColor for focus changes, CABasicAnimation on bounds/position for frame changes — both with very short durations (~120ms) and explicit '_disableActions = NSNumber(true)' guards when the user is mid-drag (live resize) so we don't double-animate. Why: Polish without cost — one-shot animations don't constitute an active draw loop. How: BorderRenderer captures previous color/frame per windowID; on apply, wraps the property change in CATransaction with duration. Live-drag detection via WindowState.isLiveDragging hint from WindowTracker (need to plumb that signal first).
acceptance_criteria: Focus changes crossfade smoothly. Frame changes tween except during live drag. Idle CPU unchanged.
